subject: Umbratek sandbox trial — proposed success metrics & kickoff next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@umbratek.com>; Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@umbratek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Umbratek sandbox trial — proposed success metrics & kickoff next steps

Hi Alex / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the primary evaluation goal (document understanding + snippet retrieval with generation). Per our discussion, I put together a concise acceptance matrix and a proposed evaluation cadence so we can move to a short sandbox trial next week. High-level items below; attached are the detailed matrix, a sample workload spec, and a draft mutual action plan.

Proposed success metrics (pass/fail thresholds):
- Latency: 99th percentile generation latency < 250 ms for 512-token context (measured over 1-hour window at target throughput).
- Throughput: sustained 180 requests/sec for 1-minute sustained bursts (95% of minute).
- Cost: avg. infra cost per 1k tokens served <= $1.90 (we'll provide cost model per configuration).
- Quality: intent classification F1 >= 0.90 on your annotated dev set; factuality/hallucination rate <= 1.5% on sample prompts.
- Accuracy guardrail: top-1 retrieval precision >= 92% for snippet candidates returned by your retriever.

Evaluation plan (timeline & owners):
- Wed 2026-09-02: Sandbox provisioned (Redwood infra) + baseline model loaded (Owner: Ben).
- Thu 2026-09-03: Smoke run with 1k synthetic queries; initial latency/throughput readouts (Owner: Redwood SE - Ben, Customer SE - Alex).
- Mon 2026-09-07: Full 48-hour trial using your replayed traffic and a 10k-sample quality bench (Owner: Umbratek QA - Priyanka; Redwood Ops - Marissa).
- Tue 2026-09-08: Readout call with pass/fail per acceptance matrix; next steps on hardening or rollout.

Operational notes / constraints:
- We'll use KV caching + continuous batching enabled by default; if you require stricter latency, we can pin smaller batch sizes for critical routes.
- Please send the annotated dev set and a 10k-sample replay by EOD Wednesday so we can pre-load perf instrumentation. The sample-workload-spec.json outlines required formats.

Next steps for you (requested):
1) Confirm acceptance thresholds above or propose adjustments.
2) Share the replay dataset link + annotated dev set.
3) Block 30 minutes on Sep 8 for the readout.

If that looks good I'll schedule provisioning for Wed and loop in infra to get the sandbox ready.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: trial-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), sample-workload-spec.json (json), mutual-action-plan.md (md)

Subject: Re: Umbratek sandbox trial — proposed success metrics & kickoff next steps

Thanks, Soojin — that summary is super helpful. We're aligned on most points; couple of adjustments from our side: 
- Latency: can we target 200 ms p99 instead of 250 ms? That's what our UX team prefers for interactive flows. If that pushes cost beyond our plan we'll flag it during the 48-hour trial.
- Throughput: we anticipate baseline peak of ~150 rps and potential spike tests up to 300 rps; happy to start the 48-hour at 180 rps as you proposed and then run a spike test on day 2.

We can share the annotated dev set and replay by EOD Wednesday — I'll put the link in Drive and share access to Redwood. Priyanka will lead QA for the 48-hour run.

Confirming Sep 8 readout — 11:00 PT works for us. Please include Ben and Marissa on the invite.

Alex
Alex Nguyen
Head of Product, Umbratek
